subject: expense-approval-reference
purpose: Try bounded Execution and Function responsibilities for the existing Expense development object.

interpretation.target: A local single-organization browser Expense system with authorized first-stage and General Manager decisions on the same current revision, rejection/revision history, and normal local restart recovery.
interpretation.historical_context: Existing model current/gap fields describe realignment before historical rejudge; they are not a present unresolved-feature list.
interpretation.original_definitions: Retained without supersession or status transfer. Proposed IDs below are local to this trial.
interpretation.existing_readers: Continue using existing five-carrier/eight-Function definitions. This trial is not wired into onboarding, assessments, replay or platform consumers.
interpretation.condition_assessment: No new condition-assessment pilot task, assessment set, composition result or path judgment is created.
scope: normal application restart against the same SQLite file
limits: no enterprise IAM or production security claim
no crash consistency, replication, backup recovery or remote durability claim

execution_loops.name: Expense business ledger core
execution_loops.implementation_entity: Expense domain and SQLite application core
execution_loops.boundary: Content validation, local role rules, state transitions, current revision checks, decisions, new revisions and business history persistence.
inputs: validated operation arguments from the service
execution_loops.note: Domain and Store remain separate internal modules within one proposed carrier; no physical refactor is proposed.

execution_loops.name: Local application service
execution_loops.boundary: API transport, JSON mapping, errors, static resource delivery, server and database-path assembly, and process lifecycle.

execution_loops.name: Browser interaction client
execution_loops.boundary: Forms, user actions, current-state presentation, request handling and history display.

execution_loops.name: Verification and raw observation tools
execution_loops.implementation_entity: Test, CI and raw application observation tooling
execution_loops.boundary: Verification environment, temporary resources, driving core/HTTP/browser/restart scenarios, and preserving raw observations.
execution_loops.note: Test expectations trace to the relevant Function contract; maintenance of test code here does not move judgment ownership into the runner.

execution_loops.name: CloseLoop handoff and frozen replay tools
execution_loops.implementation_entity: Project-owned source profile, owner bindings and public-entry replay adapter
execution_loops.boundary: Project declarations, source/owner bindings, material restoration and invocation of existing platform public interfaces.
execution_loops.note: Everything under records/, including runner/*.py, remains historical frozen material, not newly activated implementation code. E5 is not evidence that a business Function is valid.
execution_loops.maintenance_boundary: Physical maintenance of conditions/composition files covers format, bindings and references only. Their semantic criteria remain with the relevant Function authors; preservation of records does not transfer truth ownership.

shared_contracts.meaning: Submission, decisions, revisions and displayed history preserve exact business revision meaning; product Git and execution/evidence revisions remain separate.
Submitted/reviewed revisions and decisions remain traceable. Ordinary draft editing is not silently expanded into a full edit-event journal.
An invalid operation does not change the business state that its path promises to preserve.
Required user-visible actions are available through the original Chromium reference path; test execution itself is not the capability.
Normal local application restart against the same SQLite file preserves the relevant actors, revisions, states, decisions and query behavior.

function_loops.name: Expense preparation and submission
function_loops.scope: Local single-organization draft preparation and submission of the current expense revision, including its declared browser and normal-restart conditions.
function_loops.limits: No external identity provider or production security claim; the original local-actor trust question remains explicit.
function_loops.upstream_need: Existing GN1: present a definite expense revision for authorized review.
function_loops.target: An employee can create and edit legal draft content and submit the current draft revision for review.
function_loops.input: Employee identity within the declared local-actor model and expense content.
function_loops.output: A submitted expense revision with definite approval-relevant content.
function_loops.owns: Draft/content and submission capability contract, its gap and scoped path judgment.
excludes: creating a new revision after rejection

conditions.requirement: Employee and amount/purpose/receipt_ref satisfy the inherited input and actor contract.
Legal drafts can be edited; invalid edits and invalid submissions preserve business state.
Only the current draft can be submitted; expense identity, revision and submitted content are exact.
Submitted approval-relevant content cannot be edited in place; prior submitted/reviewed revisions and decisions are retained.
The employee can create, edit and submit through the browser, including visible invalid-operation handling.
Normal restart preserves the actor, current revision, submitted content and state produced by this path.

current_capability_state.description: Baseline E1/E2/E3 implement local draft creation/edit and submission; historical results remain at their original revisions.

capability_gap.description: Clarify caller/own-expense and concurrent edit/submit obligations before claiming those boundary cases.

function_loops.feedback_boundary: A condition/evidence gap leads to a bounded support, repair or clarification request to the relevant Execution carrier. Its implementation facts remain with that carrier; a new judgment needs its own basis.

function_loops.name: Two-stage authorized decision
function_loops.scope: First-stage and General Manager review of the same current local expense revision, including either-stage rejection.
function_loops.limits: Seeded local role assignments, not organizational IAM; concurrency coverage is unresolved.
function_loops.upstream_need: Existing GN1: final approval requires authorized first-stage and General Manager decisions on the same current revision.
function_loops.target: The current submitted revision traverses authorized first-stage and final review, or is rejected at either stage.
function_loops.input: Current submitted or manager_pending revision, local review actor, outcome and reason.
function_loops.output: An ordered decision chain and corresponding manager_pending, rejected or approved business state.
function_loops.owns: Review policy, stage order, decision/revision binding and scoped approval capability judgment.

conditions.requirement: First-stage review accepts only the current submitted revision and an explicit approver who is not the submitter.
First-stage approval yields manager_pending, never final approved.
Final review requires general_manager authority, completed first-stage approval and the same exact current revision.
Either review stage may reject; actor, role, outcome, reason, revision and order remain traceable.
Wrong actor/role, self-review, skipped stage, stale revision, duplicate or invalid decisions do not alter the promised business state.
Final approved content cannot be silently changed while retaining its prior approval.
Browser paths support initial and final approval/rejection and make the intermediate/final distinction visible.
Normal restart preserves review roles, stage state, both decision stages and their exact revision bindings.

current_capability_state.description: Baseline implements approver and general_manager stages, role checks, current-revision checks and persisted decisions.

capability_gap.description: The old final-review pilot does not judge this combined F2. Same-expense concurrent decision obligations remain a proposed investigation.

function_loops.feedback_boundary: A condition/evidence gap leads to a bounded support, repair or clarification request to the relevant Execution carrier. Its implementation facts remain with that carrier; a new judgment needs its own basis.

function_loops.name: New draft after rejection
function_loops.scope: New draft creation from the current revision rejected at either review stage, with explicit F1/F2 handoff coverage.
function_loops.limits: No workflow delegation or escalation rules; does not own F1 submission or F2 decisions.
function_loops.upstream_need: Existing GN1: rejection can be answered without erasing previous facts or carrying old approvals forward.
function_loops.target: A rejection at either stage can produce a legal new draft revision under the same expense.
function_loops.input: The current rejected revision and revised content.
function_loops.output: A new draft revision with old revisions and decisions preserved.
function_loops.owns: Rework eligibility, revision creation, reset of approval applicability and the new-draft handoff contract.

conditions.requirement: Only the current rejected revision may be revised; rejection from either stage is supported.
Legal revised content creates a new increasing revision under the same expense, in draft state.
Old content and decisions remain; the new draft inherits no effective approval.
Invalid or repeated revision requests do not mutate prior business state or create extra revisions.
The browser can create the new draft after either-stage rejection and hand it to F1.
Normal restart preserves new/old revisions and the rejected decision basis.

function_loops.handoff: F3 ends at the new draft. The original revise-and-resubmit promise also requires I1/I2: F1 resubmission followed by both F2 review stages.

current_capability_state.description: Baseline creates a new draft after a rejected revision and retains old revisions/decisions; existing I1/I2 source scenarios are historical.

capability_gap.description: Review I1/I2 responsibility coverage and clarify simultaneous/repeated revision obligations; this trial establishes no new execution gap finding.

function_loops.feedback_boundary: A condition/evidence gap leads to a bounded support, repair or clarification request to the relevant Execution carrier. Its implementation facts remain with that carrier; a new judgment needs its own basis.

function_loops.name: Traceable history reading
function_loops.scope: Read-only history for one expense through the local API and Chromium UI, including normal-restart availability.
function_loops.limits: No cross-expense audit dashboard; full status-event granularity and caller-read scope require clarification.
function_loops.upstream_need: Existing GN1: users can inspect versions and authorized decisions, including rejected history.
function_loops.target: The user can inspect the correct expense's revisions and ordered decisions with their revision, actor, role, outcome and reason.
function_loops.owns: History query, ordering, relation presentation and user-visible inspection capability.
excludes: silently resolving the open status-history granularity question

conditions.requirement: The queried expense and version/decision ordering are correct, without fabricated or cross-expense facts.
Decisions retain their revision, actor, role, outcome and reason; rejected history coexists with later revisions.
Valid and invalid history queries do not modify business state.
The browser exposes versions, role-attributed decisions and their relationships for inspection.
The relevant history and query behavior remain available after normal restart.

current_capability_state.description: Baseline exposes ordered revisions/decisions through the store, HTTP history route and browser.

capability_gap.description: Clarify full status-history granularity and caller/read scope; do not infer an event journal or authenticated ownership from the code.

function_loops.feedback_boundary: A condition/evidence gap leads to a bounded support, repair or clarification request to the relevant Execution carrier. Its implementation facts remain with that carrier; a new judgment needs its own basis.

original_coverage_mapping.original_limits: No external identity provider or production security claim.

original_coverage_mapping.original_scope: first-stage review of current submitted revision
original_coverage_mapping.original_limits: Local seeded role assignments only; no enterprise IAM claim.
General manager authority is local sample configuration, not organizational IAM.
No workflow delegation or escalation rules.
Only amount, purpose and receipt_ref are approval-relevant in this sample.
No crash consistency, replication or remote durability claim.

relation_design.principle: Bounded objects, many-to-many references, distinct fact ownership and per-path judgments.
relation_design.pattern: A Function record F may composes/supports/depends_on an Execution record E: source is F and target is E. Target support flows upward conceptually; it is not the typed-edge direction.
relation_design.required_binding: Any adopted relation must specify real source/target records and revisions, actor, scope, limits, reason/evidence and propagation rule.
relation_design.change_handling: Follow the adopted typed relation and relevant basis change; do not mark every path stale because any file or project node changed.
relation_design.judgment_boundary: Shared evidence or conditions never create one shared global path_state. New F2 cannot inherit the old final-approval pilot result.

open_questions.question: Does commissioned full status history require an event journal for every state transition, beyond stored revision states and ordered decisions?
open_questions.disposition: Retain the original wording and historical acceptance. Clarify the next contract before claiming complete event-history coverage.

open_questions.question: Which simultaneous requests on one expense must the reference sample handle atomically?
open_questions.disposition: Reads/checks precede some write transactions while HTTP is threaded. This is an unexecuted code-risk observation, not a defect verdict or revoked historical acceptance.

open_questions.question: How does the original employee-own-expense requirement apply to caller-supplied names and API requests without authenticated caller context?
open_questions.disposition: Keep the local named-actor limit and original requirement explicit; do not silently equate role lookup with authenticated ownership or add enterprise IAM.

review_criteria: Each active implementation path in maintained_paths has one proposed maintenance owner; shared use is an explicit dependency.
All eight original Function identities retain a visible coverage mapping with original scope/limits and no judgment transfer.
F3-to-F1-to-F2 preserves the full rejected/revise/resubmit requirement.
Browser and normal-restart conditions remain mandatory where applicable, not optional evidence labels.
Open requirements and code risks remain explicit without invented current validity.
Existing source, frozen evidence, model, consumers and pilot mode remain unchanged.

evolution_plan.execution: For a later authorized carrier change, retain implementation entity/boundary, changed scope, source revision, execution/evidence references and reproduction limits.
evolution_plan.function: Compare each path's target and current capability, request the affected support, then judge on explicit revision-bound evidence. Keep prior findings and repair responses.
evolution_plan.cross_path: Use real typed relations to determine which dependent records need rejudge; sharing a carrier does not mandate all-path rejudge.
evolution_plan.governance: Retain the existing target and historical reference-sample decision. A new applicable decision, if needed, belongs to the authorized governance actor, not this trial or a helper.
evolution_plan.next_action: Review the proposed boundaries, inherited requirement coverage and open questions before any adapter adoption or new implementation task.
